text:
adele: Heads up — multiple customers (enterprise tier) reporting p99 latency spike after we onboarded skyline3 yesterday evening. Symptoms: long-doc requests (~30–80k tokens) to /v1/chat show p95 ~1.2s -> 2.8s and p99 jumps to 8–12s. Started ~11:10pm UTC after the rollout.

maria: which route/region? any auth errors?

adele: US-EAST primarily, a couple in EU-WEST. No auth errors in support logs, but one tenant had repeated 401->retry loops due to stale API key in their client — could be amplification for that customer only.

sam: I noticed skyline3 onboarding changed the tokenizer normalization flag (unic_norm=true) and updated merge rules. That can create longer tokenized sequences for CJK + emoji heavy docs. Could cause more KV cache churn and larger attention windows.

maria: do we have a repro payload?

adele: customer sent an anonymized sample. Pasting sanitized first ~2000 chars below.

adele: ```\n<redacted long doc snippet with mixed CJK, emojis, and lots of short code blocks>\n``` 

sam: ran local repro on cpu with our tokenizer v2.3.1 vs v2.4.0 (skyline onboarding). Results: v2.4.0 tokenizes that doc to ~74k subtokens vs 62k on v2.3.1. That's +19% tokens -> more KV lookups and larger attention work per request. Also saw increased time in tokenization (sync) path.

sam: quick diff of tokenizer config:
sam: ```json
{
  "unicode_normalize": true,  // v2.4.0
  "merge_rules": "unified_v3",
  "max_bytes_per_token": 6
}
```

maria: so two sources: (1) tokenization producing more tokens -> more inference cost/latency (2) possible client retry amplification.

oliver: recommend immediate mitigations: (A) Rollback tokenizer normalization for skyline3 canary -> reduce token count. (B) Enable prefix/KV caching for long-doc customers on dedicated pools. (C) Temporarily route heavy long-doc traffic to older skyline2 model variant until onboarding issues fixed.

adele: customers asking for ETA. Can we do canary rollback quickly?

deploy-bot: Deploy 17555-skyline3-tokenizer-toggle initiated by oliver at 2025-03-04T00:45:00Z — canary 10% -> 0% rollback in progress.

sam: to reproduce internally:
sam: 1) set tokenizer to v2.4.0
sam: 2) send single /v1/chat request with our sample payload (content length ~70k chars)
sam: 3) measure token count and p95/p99 for 3 runs
sam: quick CLI:
sam: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST' \
  -d '{"model":"skyline3","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<sample-doc>"}],"max_tokens":2048}' | jq -r .usage
```

maria: thanks. I'll run against staging with both tokenizer flags and capture KV cache stats + runtime flame.

oliver: also bump observability alert to include tokenization time component in the latency breakdown so we can tell tokenization vs model inf vs postprocessing.

adele: customers requesting interim mitigation—can we flip per-tenant model pinning? Some are on Dedicated with reserved pools.

oliver: yes, we can pin tenants to skyline2 on their Dedicated pools. For Hosted customers we can create a per-tenant routing rule to prefer skyline2 until tokenization bug fixed.

sam: root cause hypothesis: unicode_normalize=true increases grapheme splitting for emoji/CJK leading to more subtoken emission + triggers a slow tokenization code path when sequences exceed 64k subtokens which disables some fast attention kernels.

maria: noted. I captured a trace: tokenization 420ms -> model prepare 80ms -> kv load 160ms -> model decode p99 tail 9s. After rollback on canary 10% -> 0% we saw one canary customer drop p99 from 11s->3.1s within 20 minutes.

adele: customer outreach: I've DM'ed affected accounts, offering to pin to skyline2 and offering credits for the incident. They're asking for timeline for full fix.

sam: plan: (1) revert unicode_normalize for skyline3 tokenizer, (2) add a deterministic normalization test for large mixed-language/emojis in unit tests, (3) optimize tokenizer fast-path for >64k subtokens or clamp pre-tokenization with a warning.

oliver: I'll own the rollback and routing changes. maria you own traces and regression test. sam you own tokenizer patch and unit tests. adele you own customer comms.

maria: starting trace collection now, will attach flame graphs to the ticket.

adele: thanks team. Will update customers: immediate pin available + ETA for patch ~48–72h depending on QA.

sam: one extra note — check billing counters: increased token counts will affect per-token billing; finance should be aware and we should consider applying retro credits for unexpectedly inflated tokens during the incident window.

adele: filed FIN ticket and support ticket linking traces.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed: skyline3 tokenizer flag reset in canary and rolled to 0% canary at 2025-03-04T01:02:10Z. Monitoring p99 for affected tenants.

maria: early numbers: p99 back to ~3s for canary-tenants. We'll keep monitoring.

adele: closing loop with customers now. Thanks everyone. :heart
